items.prompt:
A statement the author wants you to accept is a:
A) claim
B) title
C) rhyme

Evidence that does not relate to the claim is:
A) relevant
B) irrelevant
C) sufficient

Reasoning that makes logical sense is:
A) sound
B) flawed
C) irrelevant

Read.

'School should start later because teens need more sleep; a study found later-starting teens earn higher grades.'

The evidence (the study) is:
A) relevant to the claim
B) irrelevant
C) about a different topic

steps: Study supports the claim. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Read.

'We should ban all cars because my neighbor's car is ugly.'

The reasoning is:
A) sound
B) not sound (irrelevant, insufficient)
C) perfectly logical

steps: One ugly car ≠ ban all cars. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Strong evidence for a claim is:
A) relevant and sufficient
B) off-topic
C) a single rare example

Read.

'Vitamin X cures colds. I took it once and my cold went away in a week.'

Why is this argument WEAK?
A) a single personal case is insufficient, and colds go away on their own anyway
B) it uses too much data
C) the claim is irrelevant
items.answer: A) a single personal case is insufficient, and colds go away on their own anyway

steps: Insufficient, flawed reasoning. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) a single personal case is insufficient, and colds go away on their own anyway

items.prompt:
Which argument is the STRONGEST?
A) 'Recycling helps: a study of 50 cities found recycling cut landfill waste by an average of 30%.'
B) 'Recycling helps because my friend likes it.'
C) 'Recycling helps; everyone says so.'
items.answer: A) 'Recycling helps: a study of 50 cities found recycling cut landfill waste by an average of 30%.'

steps: Relevant, sufficient data. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'Recycling helps: a study of 50 cities found recycling cut landfill waste by an average of 30%.'
